assets.name: Test
assets.physicalImpactRationale: Derived from HazardItem chain: contributes [indirect] to "Fehlende Standfestigkeit" (irreversible_injury)

properties.notes: SPI-Protokoll CB-1-Seite. Empfängt Kommandos von CB-2, sendet Messdaten und Diagnosestatus. Puffert Daten bei SPI-Ausfall.
Download via P-7/WLAN, Signaturvalidierung, Flash-Write auf DS-4 (Controller) und via P-11 auf DS-2 (Sensor).
IEEE 802.11 b/g/n. Station-Modus (Update-Server) + AP-Modus (Wartung). Terminiert TLS.
RS485-Stack + Applikationsschicht. Austauschbar für 868MHz Wireless oder andere OT-Protokolle.

properties.safetyRationale: Schwellwert manipuliert = kein Alarm oder Daueralarm

properties.notes: [MIGRATED] logicalAccessControl=password — re-model on the terminating process/flow (authenticationRequired / endpointAuthentication).

threatProfile.rationale: Zugang zum Brandmeldenetz erfordert physischen Zutritt
Sehr hoher Aufwand, aber alle Geräte betroffen

properties.notes: Empfängt Firmware-Image von P-5 via SPI, schreibt in DS-2. Führt Post-Flash-Readback durch.

== Executive Summary

This document describes the threat and risk analysis for *Smoke Detector*.

=== Overview

The smoke detector is an industrial fire detector based on optical light-scattering measurement. It detects smoke particles through forward and side scattering of an LED light beam, processes the measurements locally, and transmits alarm signals to a fire alarm control panel via RS485. Configuration and firmware updates are performed via Wi-Fi.

Safety-critical characteristic: The availability and integrity of the smoke detection function are safety-critical—failure to generate an alarm in the presence of smoke can endanger human lives.

== Applicable Regulations

The following regulations and standards are applicable to this project and have been considered in the threat and risk analysis.

=== CRA

The **EU Cyber Resilience Act (CRA)** establishes mandatory cybersecurity requirements for products with digital elements throughout their entire lifecycle. Manufacturers must implement secure development practices (security by design), establish vulnerability handling processes, and provide ongoing security updates for the expected product lifetime. Key requirements include:

- Risk assessment and threat analysis during product development
- Security testing and vulnerability management
- Incident reporting within 24 hours of awareness
- Minimum 5-year security update support
- Technical documentation including SBOM (Software Bill of Materials)

This threat model addresses CRA requirements by systematically identifying and assessing security risks, documenting mitigation measures, and establishing a baseline for ongoing vulnerability management.

'''

=== IEC 62443

**IEC 62443** is the international standard series for Industrial Automation and Control Systems (IACS) security. It provides a comprehensive framework addressing security for asset owners, system integrators, and component suppliers.

Key elements relevant to this analysis:

- **IEC 62443-3-2**: Security risk assessment for system design
- **IEC 62443-3-3**: System security requirements and security levels (SL 1-4)
- **IEC 62443-4-1**: Secure product development lifecycle requirements
- **IEC 62443-4-2**: Technical security requirements for IACS components

This threat model follows IEC 62443-3-2 methodology for zone and conduit analysis and maps identified risks to appropriate Security Levels as defined in IEC 62443-3-3.

'''

info.description:
The smoke detector is an industrial fire detector based on optical light-scattering measurement. It detects smoke particles through forward and side scattering of an LED light beam, processes the measurements locally, and transmits alarm signals to a fire alarm control panel via RS485. Configuration and firmware updates are performed via Wi-Fi.

Safety-critical characteristic: The availability and integrity of the smoke detection function are safety-critical—failure to generate an alarm in the presence of smoke can endanger human lives.
info.name: Smoke Detector

risks.attackDescription: Attacker sends high volume of requests consuming all available CPU, memory, or file handles
risks.causeDescription: No resource limits or rate limiting — process allocates unbounded resources in response to requests

proposedMitigations.text: Use load balancing to distribute traffic

proposedVerifications.text: Stress testing and load testing (k6, JMeter)

risks.threatDescription: Process resource exhaustion — attacker exhausts process resources causing denial of service

risks.attackDescription: Attacker exploits a process vulnerability to execute code or trigger operations with elevated privileges
risks.causeDescription: Insufficient input validation or privilege boundary enforcement in the process

proposedMitigations.text: Implement proper ACLs and role-based access control

proposedVerifications.text: Authorization bypass testing (OWASP ZAP, Burp Suite)

risks.threatDescription: Privilege escalation via process vulnerability — attacker gains elevated privileges through process flaw

risks.attackDescription: Attacker injects requests pretending to be a legitimate caller
risks.causeDescription: Insufficient process authentication — callers are not required to prove their identity

proposedMitigations.text: Implement secure session management with proper timeout

risks.threatDescription: Process identity spoofing — attacker impersonates a legitimate process

risks.attackDescription: Attacker intercepts the response from Sensor Communication Controller to Optical Detection Controller and reads sensitive information
risks.causeDescription: Unencrypted or weakly protected response channel — response data is readable in transit

proposedMitigations.text: Encrypt data at rest using AES-256
Encrypt data in transit using TLS 1.3

proposedVerifications.text: Encryption strength verification (correct algorithms, key lengths)
Network traffic analysis for unencrypted data

risks.threatDescription: Eavesdropping on response: Attacker intercepts sensitive response data from Sensor Communication Controller

risks.attackDescription: Attacker intercepts the response from Sensor Communication Controller and modifies data, causing Optical Detection Controller to process falsified information
risks.causeDescription: Missing integrity protection on the response flow from Sensor Communication Controller — Optical Detection Controller cannot detect modified responses

proposedMitigations.text: Use digital signatures for data integrity

proposedVerifications.text: Fuzzing tests for input validation (AFL, Peach, Radamsa)

risks.threatDescription: Response tampering: Attacker modifies response data before it reaches Optical Detection Controller

risks.attackDescription: Attacker disrupts or delays the response channel from Sensor Communication Controller, causing Optical Detection Controller to stall or fail
risks.causeDescription: No redundancy or timeout protection — Optical Detection Controller depends on responses from Sensor Communication Controller to continue operation

proposedMitigations.text: Use ACLs or filtering to restrict access

proposedVerifications.text: Stress testing and load testing (k6, JMeter)

risks.threatDescription: Response blocking: Attacker prevents Optical Detection Controller from receiving responses from Sensor Communication Controller

threats.threatDescription: Response blocking: Attacker prevents Controller Communication Handler from receiving responses from Wifi Gateway

threats.attackDescription: Attacker modifies the response from Wifi Gateway to include elevated roles or permissions, causing Controller Communication Handler to grant unauthorized access
threats.causeDescription: Controller Communication Handler trusts response data from Wifi Gateway without integrity verification, enabling privilege decisions based on forged responses
threats.threatDescription: Response manipulation for privilege escalation: Attacker manipulates response to gain elevated access in Controller Communication Handler

threats.attackDescription: Attacker forges the identity of Controller Communication Handler and sends malicious data to Wifi Gateway, which processes it as legitimate
threats.causeDescription: Missing sender authentication on incoming data flow — Wifi Gateway cannot verify the true origin of received data
threats.threatDescription: Sender spoofing: Attacker impersonates Controller Communication Handler to deceive Wifi Gateway

threats.attackDescription: Attacker intercepts the data flow from Controller Communication Handler and modifies commands or payload before delivery to Wifi Gateway
threats.causeDescription: Missing integrity protection on the data flow from Controller Communication Handler — data arrives without tamper evidence
threats.threatDescription: Data tampering on incoming flow: Attacker modifies data before it reaches Wifi Gateway

threats.attackDescription: Controller Communication Handler claims it never sent the command or data that Wifi Gateway received and acted upon
threats.causeDescription: No non-repudiation mechanism on the data flow — requests from Controller Communication Handler are not signed or cryptographically bound to the sender
threats.threatDescription: Sender repudiation: Controller Communication Handler denies sending the request or data

threats.attackDescription: Attacker passively monitors the data flow and reads sensitive payload transmitted from Controller Communication Handler to Wifi Gateway
threats.causeDescription: Unencrypted or weakly protected communication channel between Controller Communication Handler and Wifi Gateway
threats.threatDescription: Eavesdropping on incoming data: Attacker intercepts sensitive data flowing to Wifi Gateway

threats.attackDescription: Attacker sends a high volume of requests via the data flow, exhausting the processing capacity of Wifi Gateway
threats.causeDescription: No rate limiting or request throttling protecting Wifi Gateway from high-volume input via Controller Communication Handler
threats.threatDescription: Request flooding: Attacker overwhelms Wifi Gateway with excessive incoming requests

threats.attackDescription: Attacker injects malicious commands or payloads into the data flow, which Wifi Gateway executes with its own privilege level
threats.causeDescription: Insufficient input validation in Wifi Gateway — incoming data from Controller Communication Handler is processed with elevated trust
threats.threatDescription: Command injection: Attacker injects commands via data flow to escalate privileges in Wifi Gateway
